title: Honma, astronomer behind black hole image, named for autumn honor
excerpt: Japan’s government said Monday that it would award Medals of Honor to 736 people and 25 organizations this fall.
content:
The government said Monday that it would award Medals of Honor to 736 people and 25 organizations this autumn, including astronomer Mareki Honma, who participated in the project that captured the first image of a black hole.

Honma, 55, professor at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan, will be awarded the Medal with Purple Ribbon, which honors those who have achieved outstanding academic, sports or artistic results.

He headed the Japanese team for the Event Horizon Telescope international research project, which succeeded in photographing a black hole by linking radio telescopes around the world.

Other awardees of the same medal include contemporary artist Yoshitomo Nara, 66, known for his depictions of girls with large, cartoon-like eyes and works featuring dogs. The government recognizes his contribution to the development of contemporary art in Japan.

Contemporary artist Yoshitomo Nara is known for his depictions of girls with large, cartoon-like eyes and works featuring dogs. | AFP-JIJI

The medal will also be awarded to Yuko Kitagawa, 66, vice president of Keio University and a specialist in surgical medicine, and Takao Someya, 58, professor of electronic engineering at the University of Tokyo.

Among those selected for the Medal with Blue Ribbon in recognition of their contributions to the promotion of industry and social welfare was Naoki Iimori, 64, head of sake producer Fukuchiyo Shuzo, known for its Nabeshima brand.

Of the 736 awardees, 160 are women. Thirteen people, including one woman, are set to receive the Medal with Purple Ribbon, while the Medal with Blue Ribbon will go to 443 people, including 132 women.
